authUrl.description:
External Postgres URL for the auth database. Auth data is kept in its
own database so it never shares a schema with application data.
authUrl.title: authUrl

url.description:
External Postgres URL for the application database. Setting this
disables the bundled Postgres.
url.title: url

domain.description:
Parent domain everything is served under. Required unless every entry in
`hosts` is set explicitly.

The session cookie is issued on this domain so the dashboard, API and auth
service all see it — which is why the three hostnames must share a parent.
domain.title: domain

existingSecret.description:
Name of a Secret you manage yourself, holding every sensitive value.

**Set this if you deploy with ArgoCD, Flux, or anything else that renders
with `helm template`.** Left empty, the chart generates the secrets it needs
on first install and reads them back on upgrade — but a GitOps renderer has
no cluster access, so it cannot read them back and will generate fresh values
on every sync. That silently rotates the session key and the integration
encryption key: everyone gets logged out and stored integration tokens stop
decrypting.

Keys read from it, when set: BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, INTEGRATION_ENC_KEY,
SLACK_LOGIN_CLIENT_SECRET, DATABASE_URL, AUTHD_DATABASE_URL, AXIOM_TOKEN and
BETTER_STACK_OTLP_ENDPOINT/BETTER_STACK_SOURCE_TOKEN when the observability
sinks below are on, CHATWOOT_HMAC_TOKEN when support identity validation is
on, and any integration secrets you enable below.
existingSecret.title: existingSecret

global.description: Global values are values that can be accessed from any chart or subchart by exactly the same name.
global.title: global

auth.description: Auth service hostname. Defaults to auth.<domain>.
auth.title: auth

pullSecrets.description: Image pull secrets, if you mirror the images somewhere private.
pullSecrets.title: pullSecrets

registry.description: Registry and org holding the three images.
registry.title: registry

tag.description: Image tag. Defaults to the chart's appVersion.
tag.title: tag

annotations.description:
Annotations applied to the Ingress. Point cert-manager at your issuer
here, e.g. cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer: letsencrypt-prod
annotations.title: annotations

className.description: IngressClass name, e.g. nginx or traefik.
className.title: className

secretName.description:
Secret holding the certificate. Empty lets cert-manager create
<release>-tls from the annotations above.
secretName.title: secretName

integrations.description:
Optional integrations. Each is off until its credentials are set, and the
app reports it as "not configured" rather than failing.

cloudflare.description:
Cloudflare Workers AI parses
mention resolves to "no action" — the rest of the product still works.
cloudflare.title: cloudflare

email.description:
Transactional email, used for organisation invitations. Without it,
invitations are logged by the auth service instead of sent.
email.title: email

webhookSecret.description: Required when Linear is enabled, for the same reason as Slack's.
webhookSecret.title: webhookSecret

signingSecret.description:
Required when Slack is enabled: the app refuses to start without it,
because the webhook handler fails closed and would drop every event.
signingSecret.title: signingSecret

integrations.title: integrations

axiom.description:
Ship every backend log record to Axiom in addition to stdout. Off by
default: stdout is the source of truth, and a self-hosted install has no
reason to point at somebody else's Axiom account. The notifbuddy cloud
deployment turns it on from iac/helmfile/values.yaml.

dataset.description: Axiom dataset records are ingested into.
dataset.title: dataset

enabled.description: Enable Axiom log shipping. Requires `token` and `dataset`.
enabled.title: enabled

token.description:
Axiom ingest token. Ignored when `existingSecret` is set, which must
then carry AXIOM_TOKEN.
token.title: token

axiom.title: axiom

otel.description:
OpenTelemetry trace export over OTLP/HTTP. Same posture as Axiom: off by
default, on for the notifbuddy cloud deployment.

endpoint.description:
OTLP HTTP ingest base URL with no signal path, e.g.
https://in.example.betterstackdata.com — the exporter appends /v1/traces.
Ignored when `existingSecret` is set, which must then carry
BETTER_STACK_OTLP_ENDPOINT.
endpoint.title: endpoint

serviceName.description: The service.name resource attribute on exported spans.
serviceName.title: serviceName

token.description:
Ingest source token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. Ignored when
`existingSecret` is set, which must then carry BETTER_STACK_SOURCE_TOKEN.
token.title: token

otel.title: otel

podAnnotations.description: Extra pod annotations, applied to all three workloads.
podAnnotations.title: podAnnotations

postgresql.description:
Bundled Postgres.

**Evaluation only.** It is a single replica with no backups, no failover and
no supported major-version upgrade path — bumping the image tag over an
existing volume leaves Postgres refusing to start, with no pg_upgrade step
to get you across. For anything you care about, run
Postgres separately (CloudNativePG is the usual answer on Kubernetes) and
set `database.url` / `database.authUrl` below, which switches this off.

pullPolicy.description:
Pull policy for the Postgres image. Separate from `image.pullPolicy`,
which applies to notifbuddy's own images: setting that to Never (to use
side-loaded images) must not stop Kubernetes pulling this one.
pullPolicy.title: pullPolicy

storage.description: Volume size for the bundled Postgres.
storage.title: storage

storageClass.description: StorageClass. Empty uses the cluster default.
storageClass.title: storageClass

postgresql.title: postgresql

slack.description:
Slack OAuth (Sign in with Slack / OIDC) — the only sign-in method, so this
is required. Typically the same Slack app as `integrations.slack` below;
add the redirect URL https://<auth host>/api/auth/callback/slack to the
app at https://api.slack.com/apps.

clientSecret.description: Slack app client secret. Ignored when `existingSecret` is set.
clientSecret.title: clientSecret

slack.title: slack

support.description:
In-app support widget. Off by default: it points customers at *our* support
inbox, which is not what you want on your own install — enable it only with
your own Chatwoot inbox.

baseUrl.description: Chatwoot origin. Leave as Cloud, or point at your own instance.
baseUrl.title: baseUrl

enabled.description: Enable the Chatwoot support widget on the dashboard.
enabled.title: enabled

hmacToken.description:
Identity validation token from Inboxes → Settings → Configuration.
Without it the reported identity is unverified. Ignored when
`existingSecret` is set, which must then carry CHATWOOT_HMAC_TOKEN.
hmacToken.title: hmacToken

websiteToken.description: Website inbox token. Public: it ships to the browser.
websiteToken.title: websiteToken

support.title: support
